---
title: "Simple simulation: one Gaussian"
subtitle: "A 2-D Gaussian oscillating vertically — SVD under noise, then under a chirp, then under amplitude modulation"
---

First numerical test of the chain on a fully controlled object: a single 2-D
Gaussian moving vertically at a known frequency. The point is to see what $U$,
$V$ and the spectrum of $V$ look like when the ground truth is known, and how
each noise source degrades them separately.

Three parts, all on the same object: fixed frequency with each noise source
isolated then combined (part 1), a 1.0 → 1.3 Hz chirp (part 2), and a fixed
1 Hz carrier whose amplitude steps down 8 → 3 → 2 px, ten periods per step
(part 3) — the case that matters here, since choroidal pulsatility is far from
stationary in amplitude over a recording.

# Phase-shifted sine waves

$$
y_i(t) = \sin(2\pi f t + \phi_i)
$$ {#eq-phase-shifted-sine}

- $\phi_i = [0 \; \pi/4 \; \pi/2 \; 3\pi/4 \; \pi]$ : phase shifts

As shown in
[Phase-shifted sines : rank 2 for any $k$](svd-temporal-signals.qmd#phase-shifted-sines-rank-2-for-any-k),
such a family is rank 2 whatever the number of signals — so at most two singular
vectors carry the motion, and everything beyond $\sigma_2$ is noise.
